title: web/src/runs/timeline.test.ts:61-63: wrong expectation for started step in a live run

question: Q-001
reason: Read web/src/runs/timeline.test.ts: lines 61-63 set want to { label: state, note: null } except for started with completed/failed/cancelled, so started with queued or running expects label "started". The unit's spec (scenario "Items, states, details and payloads") and design decision 5 require { label: "running", note: null } for those two pairs, and line 91 of the same test expects "block · running". The implementation in timeline.ts is a not-implemented stub, so nothing in production code settles it differently. The clarifier suggestion matches the spec exactly and names the frozen file, which is the only way to unfreeze it.

checked.quote: let want: { label: string; note: string | null } = { label: state, note: null };
checked.claim: The default expectation is the raw step state, so started with queued or running expects label "started".
Only the three terminal run states override the default, leaving queued and running at label "started".
The sibling test in the same file requires a started step of a running run to read "running", contradicting lines 61-63.
The specification requires label "running" for a started step of a queued or running run.

checked.quote: a `started` step of a `queued` or `running` run is `{ label: "running", note: null }`
checked.claim: Design decision 5 states the same rule the clarifier suggestion applies.
The function is still a stub throwing not implemented, so no production code settles the expectation differently.
